title: Controlling Low-Level Properties of Colorful Images
author: Dal Ben

steps.title: Install SHINE_color toolbox
steps.instruction: Download the SHINE_color toolbox from OSF or GitHub and add its folder (including all subfolders) to MATLAB's path.

steps.title: Prepare input files
steps.instruction: Place the image files (any common format) or video file (.mp4, .avi, etc.) in a dedicated folder; note that videos will be split into frames automatically.

steps.title: Launch toolbox from MATLAB
steps.instruction: Open MATLAB, then either type `SHINE_color` at the command prompt or run the toolbox script; the wizard interface will appear.

steps.title: Specify input characteristics
steps.instruction: In the wizard, indicate whether the input is a set of images or a video, and provide the path to the folder or video file.

steps.title: Choose color space and mode
steps.instruction: Select one of the three color‑space options: RGB (operate on each channel separately), HSV, or CIELab. Choose whether to work directly on RGB channels or to transform to HSV/CIELab.

steps.title: Extract video frames (if needed)
steps.instruction: If a video was selected, the toolbox automatically runs `video2frames` to extract all frames into a temporary folder.

steps.title: Transform to HSV or CIELab (if chosen)
steps.instruction: When HSV or CIELab is selected, the toolbox runs `lum2scale` to convert each RGB image to the chosen space, extracting the luminance channel (Value for HSV, L for CIELab).

steps.title: Rescale luminance to 0‑255
steps.instruction: The extracted luminance channel is rescaled: Value (originally 0‑1) or L (originally 0‑100) is linearly mapped to the 0‑255 grayscale range.

steps.title: Apply SHINE operations
steps.instruction: Select the desired SHINE functions (e.g., `lumMatch`, `matchhist`, `specMatch`, `sfPlot`, etc.) and the toolbox applies them to the 0‑255 luminance channel. When operating on RGB, each of the three channels (red, green, blue) is processed sequentially in the same way.

steps.title: Rescale luminance back
steps.instruction: After manipulation, the luminance channel is rescaled from 0‑255 back to its original range (0‑1 for HSV Value or 0‑100 for CIELab L).

steps.title: Recombine channels and convert to RGB
steps.instruction: The unchanged hue‑and‑saturation (HSV) or A‑and‑B (CIELab) channels are combined with the restored luminance channel, then the image is transformed back to RGB space.

steps.title: Reassemble video (if applicable)
steps.instruction: If the input was a video, the processed frames are recombined into a new MPEG‑4 (.mp4) video using the `frames2mpeg` function.

steps.title: Save outputs and diagnostics
steps.instruction: Manipulated images or video are saved to a folder named `SHINE_color_OUTPUT`. A subfolder `DIAGNOSTICS` receives a .txt file containing mean and standard deviation of the luminance channel before and after processing for each image (and for each RGB channel when RGB mode is used). For images only, optional diagnostic plots (luminance histogram, spatial‑frequency plot, spectrum plot) can be generated.

steps.title: Review command log
steps.instruction: A .txt log file documenting all user selections and executed functions is written to the output folder, allowing full reproducibility of the session.
